Key findings

For the Bible

  • Prov 22:17–24:22 against its source, saying by saying (renderings §8, each pair checked on the transliteration):
    "give your ears" against הַט אָזְנְךָ (3.9, [divergence]); the oldest witness, oCairo SR 1840, reads "inside your belly"
    without the papyrus's "casket" – closer to בְּבִטְנֶךָ (Prov 22:18); 1.5–6 ↔ 22:21 (ꜥn הֵשִׁיב ↔ לְהָשִׁיב); 4.4–5 ↔
    22:22; 11.13–14 and 13.8–9 ↔ 22:24–25 (the same two prohibitions in the same order); 9.10–10.5 ↔ 23:4–5 (עָשֹׂה יַעֲשֶׂה-לּוֹ כְנָפַיִם has the Egyptian verb and noun; geese against the eagle; וְאֵינֶנּוּ = 9.19); 14.5–18 ↔ 23:6–8 (snk הִתְאַוָּה =
    תִּתְאָו, the mouthful swallowed and vomited; but the victim is the poor man, not the רַע עָיִן); 23.13–17 ↔ 23:1–3
    ("the bowl that is before you" = אֶת-אֲשֶׁר לְפָנֶיךָ); 27.7 ↔ 22:20 (ketiv שלשום / qere שָׁלִשִׁים; לְךָ = n=k);
    27.16–17 ↔ 22:29.
  • The Torah's laws of the boundary, the measure and the weak: 7.12–15 ↔ Deut 19:14, 27:17 and Prov 23:10 (the
    widow's boundary – the emendation גְּבוּל אַלְמָנָה); 17.18–18.3 ↔ Lev 19:35–36, Deut 25:13–16, Prov 16:11 (Egyptian too
    has two words for the balance: פֶּלֶס וּמֹאזְנֵי; Thoth made the weights as they are the Lord's מַעֲשֵׂהוּ); 18.21–19.1 ↔
    Deut 25:14, Prov 20:10: the oipe "that takes two" against אֵיפָה וְאֵיפָה – אֵיפָה is the Egyptian loanword, and "its
    abomination" stands where the Bible says תּוֹעֲבַת יְהוָה; 18.23 "the oipe is the Eye of Re" ↔ Zech 5:6 זֹאת עֵינָם;
    24.9–17 ↔ Lev 19:14, Prov 17:5; 26.9–14 ↔ Deut 24:17–21, Prov 14:31, 19:17; 20.21–21.4 ↔ Ex 23:6–8, Deut 16:19,
    Lam 3:36; 16.5–7 (two thirds of a poor man's debt released) – a [divergence] from Deut 15's release.
  • Man as clay and straw, the god his builder (24.13–20): Gen 2:7 / 2:22 וַיִּבֶן, Job 33:6, 1 Sam 2:6–7, Eccl 3:3; 24.4
    "the heart of man is the god's nose" ↔ Gen 2:7 [divergence] (tTurin reads "the god's reward").
  • Loanwords in their own context: תֵּבָה (11.4, the coffin), אֵיפָה, חָתַם (19.21, sin sealed ↔ Job 14:17), יְאֹר,
    כֶּתֶם (18.12); and Semitic loans in Late Egyptian that take their Hebrew cognate: ꜥšq עָשַׁק, mkmr.t מִכְמֹרֶת.
  • Other: 19.11–13 ↔ Prov 27:1; 19.16–17 ↔ Prov 19:21, 16:9 (men "say", the god "does"); 19.18 "no one is free of sin"
    ↔ Prov 20:9, Eccl 7:20; 22.1–8 ↔ Prov 20:22 (the "strong superior" is a human patron one must not seek; the TLA's
    "Erlöser" behind the famous גֹאֲלָם חָזָק pairing); 6.1–12 ↔ Ps 1:3, Jer 17:5–8.

For the ancient mind

  • A land surveyor's conscience: he measures, registers, sets boundary stones, records the new Nile islands in the
    king's name, calibrates the Udjat measure; his sins are professional and so is the punishment (the cheat's son is not
    enrolled as a scribe, 17.14; one stolen furrow shortens your life; the Moon lassoes the man who "hunts" a field).
  • The two men: the "hot" man whose tree is floated away and burned, the "silent" man whose tree flourishes in its own
    garden; burial is the measure of a life. Silence is power (the real crocodile does not roar; whoever "knows how to
    sleep" wins).
  • Measures as divine eyes: the Udjat is Horus's healed eye, the oipe the Eye of Re; Thoth's baboon heart is the plummet
    of every market balance – the judgement of the dead in every transaction.
  • Taboo becomes ethics (bw.t, a cult taboo, becomes the god's horror of lies); "no one is sinless", in a culture whose
    dead say "I have not sinned" forty-two times.
  • Life as a Nile voyage: the tongue is the steering oar, the Lord of All the pilot; the ferry is a moral place (take the
    fare from the rich, let the poor cross free).
  • Wealth behaves like a living thing: it does not sleep at your house, it sinks into the Duat or grows wings.
  • The book speaks about itself (it pleasures, teaches, purifies); tTurin is a school tablet with "day 4", "day 8" in
    its margins – a pupil's daily stint; one copyist, Senu son of Pamiu ("the cat"), handed down the only complete text.

Decisions taken (minor, by me; all recorded in renderings §10)

  • The refrain lines fixed by their first copies (§7, list above). Correction of the pre-set §6/§8: the "better"
    saying is not a four-line refrain – 9.5 and 16.11 differ in the Egyptian; only 9.6–8 = 16.12–14. The refrain of
    22.1–8 / 23.8–11 is four lines (22.5–8 = 23.8–11).
  • All translators' proposals merged as §10.1–10.5 (about 120 lemmas: ꜥn הֵשִׁיב, ḫꜣꜥ עָזַב, shꜣ עִוֵּת, mj.t דֶּרֶךְ /
    wꜣ.t אֹרַח, the ship words one each, twr split by construction …); jr X = הִנֵּה X (§3a amended); ḫpr future
    יִהְיֶה (§4.4); כֶּתֶם added to the loanwords.
  • Cross-language collisions: the Akkadian corpora's cognate reservations (עבר for ebēru …) bind Akkadian words;
    an Egyptian word takes the Hebrew of its meaning (§10.1.8) – but not a loanword or rare technical word that is
    another corpus's cognate     (ꜥḥwtj אָרִיס → חוֹכֵר, since אָרִיס < errēšu, §10.3.2). Common Semitic vocabulary
    (אַלְמָנָה, שֵׁכָר, מִדָּה, טִיט, תֶּבֶן, כָּבֵד) is shared: [cognate] in an Akkadian line, [equivalent] in an
    Egyptian one (§10.7.4). rwḏ.w סוֹכֵן kept (a sense word in its other corpora too).
  • Gates widened (never the Hebrew bent): the חם gate no longer reads לחם "bread" as the hot man; the "better"
    formula no longer fires on the r of ḥr-r-rʾ; יאור licensed by the spelling jwtwr; כתם gated, licensed by the
    group writing kꜣ~tj~mt.
  • The translators' philological open points (4.10 bgꜣ, 9.20, 10.9, 12.2, 14.11–12, 17.1, 18.5, 21.13, 27.1, 26.9) stay
    marked ? / in italics with the alternatives in the apparatus – decided as the most defensible reading (guidelines
    §6.8, a crux), not questions for the user.

Lessons for the guidelines, sources and tools

  • Tools: (1) An AED/TLA alternative-analysis separator can span several words: a converter must not print it as a
    lacuna; check every […] inside a line against the TLA's German before the first line (tools.md, egypt_tools.py).
    (2) A Hebrew → lemma-ids report (from the פירוק bullets) catches collisions at once: the ship words collided across
    two translators and were found only at the fourth ship word; the consistency reviewer's scratch script did it for the
    whole text (2,338 words) – worth a egypt_tools.py lexmap command, and the same for every corpus tool.
    (3) verify should warn on heavily vocalized > lines (the ★ plene rule broke again on a first save).
    (4) Short gates (two-letter roots with up to three prefix letters) hit preposition + homograph (בלחם); formulas keyed
    on a one-letter word need boundaries that exclude compounds (ḥr-r-rʾ).
    (5) check_bible_quotes.py reads a bare "ch:v" after a backticked Hebrew word as Genesis.
  • Guidelines §5.2: (1) The cognate rule across languages needs its scope stated: it protects loanwords and rare
    technical words (אָרִיס), not the common Semitic vocabulary that every corpus uses for its own word (§10.7.4 here).
    (2) A pre-set refrain list must be checked against the transliteration of both copies (Amenemope's "better" saying
    and its patron refrain were both mis-delimited in the pre-set renderings). (3) "Read the rank-3/5 translation only
    after drafting" also means: write its wording only with the source open. (4) A passage that will be fixed by its first
    copy should be drafted with both copies' contexts open. (5) The pattern worked: two translators, one per half, each
    resumed part by part; three fresh reviewers – the fidelity reviewer found the one systematic error.
  • Sources: the BM papyrus photographs for the line ends of 27.17–28.1.

Cross-corpus splits left for the lead

  • Shared common-Semitic words (Egyptian [equivalent], Akkadian [cognate]): אַלְמָנָה (ḫꜣr.t / almattu), שֵׁכָר
    (ḥnq.t / šikaru), מִדָּה (dbḥ / maddattu), טִיט (ꜥmꜥ.t / ṭiṭṭu), תֶּבֶן (dḥꜣ / tibnu), כָּבֵד (dns / kabtu) –
    kept by my ruling (§10.7.4); the lead may confirm it for every corpus.
  • סוֹכֵן: AM rwḏ.w, Gudea aĝrig, the Advice šatammu – three source words, all by sense.
  • חוֹכֵר (AM ꜥḥwtj) chosen to leave אָרִיס to errēšu.
  • מִכְמֹרֶת (AM mkmr.t, a Semitic loan) = the cross-corpus מִכְמֹרֶת of kamāru – one word, as it should be.
  • The other Egyptian projects (MK, MT, PT, HC) should follow AM's §10 words where they share lemmas (nṯr, ꜥnḫ, mꜣꜥ.t,
    jb / ḥꜣ.tj, the boat words, ḫpr, qd, ꜥmꜥ.t).
